title: VentureForGood (VFG) Grant
frequency: Open throughout the year; evaluation cycle takes roughly 13-24 weeks from submission to Grant Committee pitch
eligibility_citizenship: No citizenship requirement stated, but the social enterprise must be (or intend to be) registered in Singapore under the Companies Act or Co-operative Societies Act and must be a registered raiSE Social Enterprise member at the point of pitching
eligibility_note: Now targets growth-stage social enterprises (registered entities with a validated model). Very early or unregistered founders should look at raiSE's EnergiSE Grant (up to S$50,000 for impact start-ups) or join raiSE membership first. Registered raiSE membership is mandatory before pitching.
offering_description: raiSE's flagship funding scheme for Singapore social enterprises, providing up to S$300,000 to scale a revenue-generating business that addresses a social gap, evaluated by a Grant Committee after a pitch.
application_instructions: Email your pitch deck and management accounts to vfg@raise.sg (no portal). Include ACRA profile, up to 2 years of management accounts, 2-year financial projections, and founding-team resumes. Shortlisted members go through first meeting, final evaluation, then pitch to the Evaluation Committee.

questions.label: Social gap identified: clear articulation of social needs and goals (evidence-based preferred)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Name the specific unmet social need in Singapore with data or evidence, and state the goal your venture exists to achieve.

questions.label: Proposed solution: how the solution can address the problem above
questions.ai_draft_hint: Describe the product or service and draw a direct causal line from what it does to how it closes the social gap.

questions.label: Target beneficiary group/community: an in-depth understanding of their needs
questions.ai_draft_hint: Show first-hand insight into who the beneficiaries are, their lived situation, and what they actually need — not just demographics.

questions.label: Business model: USP (unique selling proposition); market size, target customer segment, current market landscape, key partners (current and planned)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Explain how the venture makes money, what makes it different from alternatives, and the realistic size of its market with named partners.

questions.label: Financial projections (2 years): key revenue streams, capital and operating expenditure, requested funding quantum, and breakdown
questions.ai_draft_hint: Give a credible 2-year P&L outline, state exactly how much you are requesting, and itemise what the grant will pay for.

questions.label: Founding team: experience in relevant industries and working with target beneficiaries; motivations — why do you want to address this need?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Pair each founder's relevant track record with a genuine personal reason for tackling this problem.

title: DBS Foundation Grant (Social Enterprise / SME track)
frequency: Annual cycle (2026 window closed 13 Jul; next cycle expected ~Q2 2027)
eligibility_citizenship: No personal citizenship requirement; business must be a registered for-profit legal entity in Singapore, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia or Taiwan
eligibility_note: For-profit entities only — individuals, sole proprietorships, non-profits and charities are ineligible. Requires ~2 years of track record delivering measurable social impact in essential needs or financial inclusion. 2026 window closed; catalogued for the next cycle.
offering_description: DBS Foundation's annual grant of up to SGD 250,000 (no equity taken) for social enterprises and impact SMEs to scale their business and social impact, with milestone-based disbursement.
application_instructions: Single online application form per entity (no save function — prepare answers offline using the Word template on the grants page, then paste into the online form). Shortlisted applicants submit a pitch deck, financials and recommendation letters, then finalists pitch to a judging panel.

questions.label: Elevator pitch of your business — Purpose: why did you start this business and what social problem are you trying to solve? Unique value proposition: what is your solution and how is it meaningfully different? Business model: revenue drivers, target customer segment, cost structure, sales channels (max 2,500 characters)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Cover all three sub-parts in order — origin/problem, differentiated solution, and how the business actually makes money — within 2,500 characters.

questions.label: What is your theory of change? Explain the solution ("We do X (Activities) to deliver Y (Outputs), which enables beneficiaries to achieve Z (Outcomes)"), the long-term outcomes/impact you intend to create, and how you track and measure impact (max 2,000 characters)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Use the X-activities to Y-outputs to Z-outcomes chain explicitly and name concrete impact metrics and how they are collected.

questions.label: Who are your core team members? Describe the relevant industry, business and impact-related experience and skill sets of the management team and advisors, plus company headcount (max 1,500 characters)
questions.ai_draft_hint: List each key person with their most relevant credential for this venture; include advisors and total headcount.

questions.label: Describe your business plans and priorities for the coming 2 years (max 1,500 characters)
questions.ai_draft_hint: State 2-3 concrete growth priorities for the next 24 months with rough timelines, tied to both revenue and impact.

questions.label: How will the grant be used to scale your business and impact? Provide a detailed breakdown, state how your target segment will benefit, and how you plan to scale after the grant is utilised (max 2,000 characters)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Itemise the budget by use, connect each line to a beneficiary-facing outcome, and explain post-grant sustainability.

questions.label: Estimated number of individuals you plan to directly reach with the grant, plus total individuals impacted to date
questions.ai_draft_hint: Give a single defensible number derived from your delivery capacity under the grant plan, consistent with your impact-to-date figure.

org_name: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment
title: SG Eco Fund — Sprout Category
frequency: Three Sprout windows per year (deadlines 30 Apr, 31 Aug, 31 Dec)
eligibility_citizenship: Individuals: Singapore Citizen or PR, 18+, residing in Singapore. Teams: all 18+ residing in Singapore, at least one Citizen/PR.
eligibility_note: Open to individuals and informal teams — no company registration needed for Sprout. Project must advance environmental sustainability in Singapore, engage the community, and have specific numerical targets (projects without measurable targets are not considered).
offering_description: The national fund for ground-up environmental sustainability projects, funding individuals, informal teams and organisations to run community-engaging green projects.
application_instructions: Apply via the government grants portal (apply.gov.sg — search 'SG Eco Fund') with Singpass. Submit a proposal deck of max 15 slides using the official template by the window deadline; shortlisted applicants may pitch for 10 minutes.

questions.label: What is the objective of your project? What environmental problem does it address and what solution will you implement?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Name one concrete environmental problem in Singapore and the specific intervention you will run against it.

questions.label: Who is your target audience and where will this take place? How will it involve and/or benefit the community?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Specify the neighbourhood/venue and how residents actively participate rather than just observe.

questions.label: Implementation plan: project duration, each activity/phase with estimated dates, and persons involved and their roles
questions.ai_draft_hint: Break the project into dated phases and assign each activity to a named team member, partner or vendor.

questions.label: Key project outcomes — environmental target (e.g. reduce food waste by xx kg) and how you will measure it
questions.ai_draft_hint: Commit to a single numerical environmental metric and a practical measurement method; projects without a clear numerical target are not considered.

questions.label: Key project outcomes — community engagement targets (e.g. xx workshops, xx volunteers) and how you will measure them
questions.ai_draft_hint: Set countable engagement outputs (sessions run, attendees) with a stated counting method like attendance lists.

questions.label: Ensuring success: external support/approvals needed and secured? Key challenges and mitigations? How is the project sustained or scaled beyond the funding period?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Address approvals/permits status, one or two realistic risks with mitigations, and a post-grant continuation plan.

title: SG Strong Fund
amount_display: Up to 90% of project cost, capped at S$7,000
frequency: Rolling — enquiry answered within ~2 days, outcome within ~1 month
eligibility_citizenship: At least 18 years old and residing in Singapore
eligibility_note: Specifically for ground-up, volunteer-led, unregistered teams whose initiative benefits local vulnerable communities. Funding covers project costs and limited stipends (max 20%). 50% disbursed upfront.
offering_description: A philanthropic fund financing informal, volunteer-led ground-up projects serving vulnerable communities in Singapore, with a lightweight enquiry-first application process.
application_instructions: Submit a grant enquiry via the form at majurity.sg/sgstrong; the grants team responds within ~2 days and arranges a short call, after which eligible applicants receive the full application form.

questions.label: Organisation/team name
questions.ai_draft_hint: Give the informal group's working name as used in the community.

questions.label: Brief overview of your organisation/team
questions.ai_draft_hint: In 2-3 sentences, say who the volunteers are, how long the group has been active, and its mission for vulnerable communities.

questions.label: Brief overview of your proposed project
questions.ai_draft_hint: Summarise the project, the vulnerable community it benefits, rough cost, and timeline — enough to gauge fit before the exploratory call.

title: Social Enterprise Community Urban Farm (SECUF) Grant
amount_display: Up to S$50,000 per enterprise (programming); up to S$500,000 per site (infrastructure)
frequency: Rolling, first-come-first-served, until 31 March 2028 or funds exhausted
eligibility_citizenship: Singapore-registered social enterprises that are raiSE members
eligibility_note: Must be a raiSE Social Enterprise member (or have concrete plans to become one within 12 months). Programming grant requires minimum 120 unique participants; infrastructure grant requires a tendered site and 5-year commitment. Best suited to founders who have registered a social enterprise.
offering_description: NParks co-funds social enterprises to set up and run community urban farms and deliver gardening programmes for seniors, persons with special needs and low-income families — the grant behind City Sprouts' community farms.
application_instructions: Stage 1: submit the interest form (go.gov.sg/secuf-interestform) for eligibility assessment, then the full proposal with target communities, programme schedule, cost breakdown and outreach plan. Reimbursement after project completion.

questions.label: Name of Social Enterprise (ACRA-registered business name)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Use the exact ACRA-registered entity name.

questions.label: Is your Social Enterprise a member of raiSE — or are there plans within the next 12 months to become one?
questions.ai_draft_hint: raiSE membership is a hard eligibility requirement; if not yet a member, state a concrete timeline.

questions.label: Tell us more about your organisation and your plans in relation to the SECUF Grant
questions.ai_draft_hint: Cover the intended farm/programme concept, target communities (seniors, persons with special needs, low-income families), expected participant numbers, and whether you seek programming or infrastructure support.

title: Young ChangeMakers (YCM) Grant
frequency: Year-round; decisions at the monthly YCM Open Mic (first Saturday of each month)
eligibility_citizenship: Singapore Citizen or PR youths aged 15-35, residing locally; teams majority SC/PR
eligibility_note: For individuals or informal youth groups — projects under a registered company are not fundable. Complete within 6 months. Standard cap S$3,000; up to S$5,000 for exceeding merit; themed tracks (Heritage, Sport, City in Nature) go up to S$7,000-8,000. Under-21 team leads need an endorsement letter.
offering_description: Seed funding of up to 100% of supported costs for youth-initiated community projects, decided by a panel of Youth Curators, plus assigned mentors and networking with other youth teams.
application_instructions: Apply via the OurSG Grants Portal (Singpass) at least 8 weeks before the 1st Saturday of your implementation month. Shortlisted teams pitch at the monthly YCM Open Mic; results within a week of pitching.

questions.label: Share how your project team came together — your team's backgrounds, experiences, and what motivated you to embark on this project
questions.ai_draft_hint: Tell a short origin story linking each member's lived experience or skills to the community problem, ending with the shared motivation.

questions.label: Provide a detailed timeline of your project, including all activities (publicity, pre-event workshops, dry-runs; for arts projects, production and show dates)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Present a month-by-month plan covering publicity, prep, delivery and wrap-up within the 6-month project window.

questions.label: Describe your project's publicity plans
questions.ai_draft_hint: Name specific channels, content formats, timing and reach targets, matched to where the target audience actually is.

questions.label: List the partners you have reached out to or intend to reach out to (partner, nature of partnership — funding/in-kind/publicity/audience access — and status)
questions.ai_draft_hint: List each partner with what they contribute and an honest status (confirmed / pending / will reach out).

title: Youth Action Grant (YAG)
frequency: Two application cycles per year; shortlisted teams pitch at Impact, IRL with public participatory budgeting
eligibility_citizenship: Singapore Citizen or PR youths aged 15-35
eligibility_note: Open to informal ground-up groups (min 2 people) and youth-led organisations incorporated up to 5 years. For projects ready to scale for sustained impact — not one-off events. Minimum project budget S$10,000; funded elements complete within 2 years. Successor to the Youth Action Challenge.
offering_description: Up to S$70,000 (100% of supported costs) to scale youth-led community projects with sustained, measurable impact — plus project guidance, capability-building workshops and a changemaker community.
application_instructions: Apply via the OurSG Grants Portal during a window with a proposal deck answering the YAG supplementary questions, budget, and team particulars; shortlisted teams pitch at Impact, IRL.

questions.label: What problem(s)/gap(s) are you trying to address? Why is it important? How do you plan to address each gap, and how does your project complement or improve on existing solutions?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Structure per gap: the gap, its impact (with evidence), your intervention, and how it differs from existing solutions.

questions.label: Share how your project team came together — backgrounds, experiences, and motivations
questions.ai_draft_hint: Emphasise track record and complementary skills — YAG assesses readiness to scale, not just passion.

questions.label: Provide a detailed timeline of your project including all activities (publicity, workshops, dry-runs)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Give a dated activity plan across the full (up to 2-year) funded period, including publicity and preparation milestones.

questions.label: Logic model: set out your programme's Inputs, Activities, Outputs, Outcomes and Impact
questions.ai_draft_hint: Draft a five-part logic model where each output flows from activities and each outcome is a measurable change in participants.

questions.label: KPIs & deliverables: mid-point milestone and end-point deliverables by target month — what you're doing, how much (output numbers), and what difference it makes (outcome percentages)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Give specific # outputs and % outcome targets at a mid-point and end-point month; avoid vague targets.

questions.label: Potential risks or challenges: each risk, its impact on the project, and specific actionable mitigations
questions.ai_draft_hint: Pick 3-4 genuine risks (recruitment, partner fallout, budget overrun) and pair each with a concrete mitigation.

questions.label: (For grant requests of S$30,000+) Follow-up plan for the project to continue, plus learning points from similar past projects
questions.ai_draft_hint: Show how the project keeps running after the grant — revenue, partners, volunteer pipeline — and cite lessons from comparable past work.

title: NYC Microgrant
frequency: Year-round, fully online, no pitch required
eligibility_note: New in 2026 under the SG Youth Plan. Covers 100% of supported costs. Designed for first-time changemakers taking an idea to first action — the easiest entry point into grant funding.
offering_description: A micro seed grant of up to S$1,000 with a simplified, no-pitch application to help youths take the first step from idea to action on a community project.
application_instructions: Register interest via NYC's online form (Singpass); NYC's Partnership Lab team follows up on next steps. Simplified applications also accepted at Impact, IRL events.

title: YCM — Youth Heritage Kickstarter Fund
frequency: Year-round; decisions at the monthly YCM Open Mic
eligibility_citizenship: Singapore Citizen or PR youths aged 15-35, residing locally; teams majority SC/PR
eligibility_note: Projects must be relevant to Singapore's heritage/history, engage the community, and complete within 6 months. Formats include mini exhibitions, guided tours, workshops, screenings, murals and temporary outdoor artwork. Projects lacking heritage elements may still be considered for the base YCM grant.
offering_description: Enhanced YCM track co-presented by NHB and NYC: seed funding of up to S$7,000 plus curator mentorship for youth-led projects that promote appreciation of Singapore's heritage.
application_instructions: Apply via the YCM grant card on the OurSG Grants Portal, selecting 'Culture & Heritage' as the category, at least 8 weeks before your implementation month; shortlisted teams pitch at the monthly Open Mic.

questions.label: Share how your project team came together — backgrounds, experiences, and motivations
questions.ai_draft_hint: Connect the team's personal connection to the heritage subject (neighbourhood, tradition, craft) with the skills to deliver it.

questions.label: Explain how your project qualifies for the Youth Heritage Kickstarter Fund: promoting appreciation and understanding of Singapore's heritage
questions.ai_draft_hint: Name the specific Singapore heritage/history the project engages and how the audience will appreciate it better afterwards.

questions.label: Provide a detailed timeline including all activities (publicity, workshops, dry-runs; production and show dates for arts formats)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Lay out a dated plan fitting the 6-month completion requirement, including research, production and public engagement phases.

questions.label: Describe your project's publicity plans
questions.ai_draft_hint: Specify channels and outreach numbers; publicity materials must credit NHB/NYC and be sent for review before release.

questions.label: List partners you have reached out to or intend to (partner, nature of partnership, status)
questions.ai_draft_hint: Name site owners, community groups, museums or grassroots partners with realistic confirmation status.

org_name: Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth
title: SG Partnerships Fund (Seed)
amount_display: Up to S$5,000 (Seed); larger tiers up to S$1M
frequency: Seed tier: year-round; decisions in ~4 weeks; up to 50% disbursed upfront
eligibility_citizenship: Singapore Citizen or PR residing in Singapore (individuals/ground-up groups via Singpass), or Singapore-registered organisations
eligibility_note: New S$50m fund launched at Budget 2026 — MCCY's flagship community ground-up grant. No age band, so youth founders qualify. Not-for-profit projects only; one active funded project at a time; declare all other funding sources.
offering_description: Year-round seed funding of up to S$5,000 (100% of eligible costs) for individuals and ground-up groups piloting new community projects, with a simplified 15-minute application and ~4-week decision.
application_instructions: Apply anytime via the SGPF (Seed) card on the OurSG Grants Portal using Singpass, with a project proposal and the SGPF Seed budget template.

questions.label: Describe your project: what it is, why the community needs it, and what will happen
questions.ai_draft_hint: A concise proposal written for a 15-minute application form — what, why, and how.

questions.label: Objective: does your project aim to benefit the community and do good, without making a profit?
questions.ai_draft_hint: State the community benefit plainly and make explicit that the project is not-for-profit — commercial projects are ineligible.

questions.label: Who it helps: does your project involve, engage, or benefit other people in Singapore?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Identify the specific community segment and estimate how many people will be involved or reached.

questions.label: How it will happen: clear steps, roles, a realistic budget, and achievable goals
questions.ai_draft_hint: Sequence the steps with owners and dates; keep budget lines within supportable categories (venue, catering, marketing, equipment, professional fees, insurance).

questions.label: Declare all other funds and/or grants you have applied for or received for this project
questions.ai_draft_hint: List every other funding source honestly — the grant offsets the project deficit, so other income reduces the eligible amount.

title: Presentation and Participation Grant
amount_display: Up to S$100,000 per financial year (up to 70% of project costs)
frequency: Three cycles a year (mid-April, mid-August, mid-December deadlines)
eligibility_citizenship: Singapore Citizens or PRs; informal collectives with majority SC/PR members; registered organisations
eligibility_note: Open to individuals AND informal collectives — collectives nominate one member to take legal/financial responsibility. Project must not have started before applying, must have a clear arts component, and be intended for public consumption. Priority to self-employed arts practitioners.
offering_description: NAC's main project grant for emerging artists and collectives: co-funds performances, exhibitions, music EPs/albums, festivals and co-creative projects with the public, in physical and/or digital formats.
application_instructions: Submit via the OurSG Grants Portal by 23:59 SGT on the cycle deadline, with the proposal and budget templates from the portal, CVs, work samples for first-time applicants, and complete scripts for theatre/literary projects.

questions.label: Is the concept well thought through and planned? Is the project original, innovative and creative?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Lead with the single artistic idea, then show concrete planning detail and what makes the treatment fresh compared to similar local work.

questions.label: Does the project encourage and promote new Singapore work?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Name the new Singapore-created works, Singaporean artists and local content the project premieres or develops.

questions.label: Does the project engage your target audience/community and reach new audiences, including those who don't normally engage in the arts?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Define audience segments with numbers and the mechanisms (free programmes, community venues, co-creation) that pull in non-arts audiences — this criterion carries the most weight.

questions.label: Do you have a clear plan to execute the project (resources, partners) and the necessary experience (artistic, production, project management, marketing)?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Map each execution function to a named team member or partner; young collectives should lean on mentors, past productions and confirmed venue partners.

questions.label: Do you have sufficient knowledge and skills to manage the project's finances and administration?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Point to a realistic itemised budget and who tracks spending — inflated budgets cast doubt on the whole proposal.

title: Creation Grant
frequency: Annual single cycle (2026 closed; next expected ~May 2027)
eligibility_citizenship: Singapore Citizens or PRs; for collaborations the lead applicant must be SC/PR
eligibility_note: For artists with a track record — 60% of assessment is artistic merit, so it suits emerging-to-mid-career artists more than first-timers. Supports up to 18 months of creation ending in a script/score/recording/exhibition/prototype plus a mini-showcase.
offering_description: Funds the research-and-development phase of an original new work — collaborator fees, residencies, workshops, experimentation and a mini-showcase to producers and presenters.
application_instructions: Submit via the OurSG Grants Portal during the annual window with the proposal and budget templates, CV, and supporting documents on past works.

questions.label: How strong and innovative is the project? Does it push artistic boundaries, and how relevant are the ideas in the wider social context?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Articulate the artistic risk being taken and connect the work's themes to a current conversation in Singapore society.

questions.label: How does the project develop your artistic practice? Is it potentially scalable for different platforms and audiences?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Frame the project as the next deliberate step in your artistic trajectory and sketch future platforms (tour, digital, adaptation).

questions.label: How does the project contribute to the art form's development and the arts scene? Does it address a critical gap in the arts ecosystem?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Name the specific gap (form, language, community, capability) in Singapore's arts ecosystem this work fills, with evidence.

questions.label: Your track record of artistic achievement and production, including critical recognition in Singapore or internationally
questions.ai_draft_hint: List strongest completed works, presentations, awards, reviews or selections chronologically — concrete recognition beats adjectives.

questions.label: Is the proposal well-planned with the resources needed to create the work on time and within budget? Is the work at a stage where you can realistically execute and launch it publicly?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Show a phased timeline with milestones, named collaborators, and evidence the work is already past pure concept stage.

questions.label: Who are you trying to reach with the eventual work, and what is your plan to market it and engage target audiences?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Describe the target audience for the finished work and the pathway to public launch — presenters, publishers or platforms already in conversation.

title: Heritage Grants — Minor Project Grant
amount_display: Up to S$50,000 (up to 80% of qualifying costs)
frequency: Twice a year (windows 4 Mar-15 Apr and 4 Aug-15 Sep); free Heritage Grants Clinics help applicants prepare
eligibility_citizenship: Singapore Citizen or PR aged 18+, residing in Singapore; non-profits, interest groups, schools; informal groups via a nominated individual
eligibility_note: Explicitly designed for first-timers with little heritage project experience. Informal groups qualify by nominating an individual to take legal/financial responsibility. Funding raised from 50% to 80% of costs from April 2026. Reserve at least 8 weeks for NHB content vetting before launch.
offering_description: Co-funds community-initiated heritage projects — trails, exhibitions, publications, documentaries, heritage spaces — that promote learning about Singapore's history and shared heritage.
application_instructions: Apply via the OurSG Grants Portal (NHB Minor Project Grant) by 23:59 on the closing date, with a project proposal (max 2,000 words), budget form, and team CVs.

questions.label: What kind of project do you have in mind? Explain the central idea, the scale, and the components involved.
questions.ai_draft_hint: State the heritage topic, output format (trail, exhibition, film, publication) and scale in the first two sentences, then break down each component.

questions.label: What do you plan to achieve? How does your project address the grant's objectives, and does it address gaps in the heritage ecosystem?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Tie objectives to the scheme's aims (learning Singapore's history, neighbourhood heritage, connecting communities) and name a specific under-documented topic.

questions.label: How will your project promote understanding, learning and discovery of Singapore's heritage and identity?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Describe the learning experience from the participant's point of view and how historical content will be researched and verified.

questions.label: What will success look like, and how will you measure the outcomes?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Give 2-3 measurable targets (attendance, downloads, survey results) plus one qualitative outcome.

questions.label: Detailed project schedule with key milestones and dates — and any potential derailers your team needs to cater for
questions.ai_draft_hint: Build a month-by-month timeline and explicitly reserve 8+ weeks for NHB content vetting before launch, plus contingency for permits.

questions.label: Who forms the project team and what are their roles? Which vendors will you appoint and for what services?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Assign each person a named role with relevant experience; keep vendors clearly separate from the project team.

questions.label: Who are your target audiences, how many people do you hope to reach, how will you publicise the project, and what will audiences gain?
questions.ai_draft_hint: Be specific about segments, give a numeric reach target, and name concrete channels — outreach is a large share of the assessment.
